3. Let S be the set of x where this attainment for ζ fails or the lower-density bound Θ(x) ≥ η₀ fails. Then μ(S) = 0 (ae_iff applied to the conjunction of two a.e. properties). Take a Borel N ⊇ S with μ(N) = 0 (exists_measurable_superset_of_null; this is toMeasurable in step 4). Put M₀ := ℝ^P ∖ N. Then M₀ is Borel, μ(ℝ^P ∖ M₀) = 0, and every x ∈ M₀ has attainment and Θ(x) ≥ η₀. Step 7's condition {|ζ|* = 1} is folded into M₀ here; with |ζ|* ≤ 1, attainment is equivalent to |ζ|* = 1. (step 4)
4. vitali_finite(P, n, μ, A := M₀, η := η₀) gives μHE[n](M₀) < ∞. (step 5)
5. rn_carrier(P, μ, ν := μHE[n], M₀) applies: μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, M₀ is Borel, μHE[n](M₀) < ∞, μ(M₀ᶜ) = 0, and the null-set hypothesis holds. It gives a Borel M ⊆ M₀ and a Borel θ with θ > 0 on M and μ = (μHE[n]⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ). This is the supplied carrier M₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} with θ = h.toReal. (steps 6–8)
6. Hence:
   - M is Borel, and μHE[n](M) ≤ μHE[n](M₀) < ∞;
   - θ is Borel and ζ is strongly measurable;
   - the measure identity holds, and θ > 0 on M;
   - |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| holds everywhere;
   - attainment and Θ(x) ≥ η₀ hold at every x ∈ M, because M ⊆ M₀. (step 10)
7. For every test form ω (step 9):
   - Γ(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ = ∫ζ(ω)dμ (integral_congr_ae, using ζ = ξ a.e.).

subproblems.title: Dual coefficient norm on n-vectors: continuous, nonnegative, dominating, and attained on the unit covector ball
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there is a function N from n-vectors to ℝ with the following properties. Here n-vectors are the continuous linear functionals ζ on the space Λⁿ(ℝ^P) of n-covectors (MultiVector P n, with the operator-norm topology), and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2} with (e_i) the standard basis of ℝ^P. (i) N is continuous; (ii) N(ζ) ≥ 0 for every ζ; (iii) |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)·|α| for every n-vector ζ and every n-covector α; (iv) for every n-vector ζ there is an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(β) = N(ζ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ N : MultiVector P n → ℝ, Continuous N ∧ (∀ ζ : MultiVector P n, 0 ≤ N ζ) ∧ (∀ (ζ : MultiVector P n) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ζ α| ≤ N ζ * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ζ : MultiVector P n, ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζ β = N ζ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: selected proof, step 1 (dual norm |ζ|* := sup{ζ(β) : |β| ≤ 1}). Step 1 only mentions the linear algebra; it is filled in here. covectorEuclideanNorm is a norm on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors, definiteness follows from multilinearity and alternation, the unit ball is compact, and the supremum is attained. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration cbr_ci_dr_multivector_dual_norm (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.cycle_im-a1.density_rep-a1.dual_norm-a1, accepted candidate 23956c44), whose frozen Lean type is byte-identical. The argument below proves its statement.

Notation:
- V := Λⁿ(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n, with its operator norm ‖·‖.
- e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).
- For J : Fin n → Fin P, e_J := (e_{J(1)}, …, e_{J(n)}).
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{J strictly increasing} α(e_J)²).
An n-vector ζ is a continuous linear functional on V; MultiVector P n carries the operator norm and its topology.

1. Coordinate bound. Let I be strictly increasing. Then α(e_I)² is one of the nonnegative summands defining |α|². Hence α(e_I)² ≤ Σ_J [J strictly increasing] α(e_J)² (Finset.single_le_sum), and |α(e_I)| = √(α(e_I)²) ≤ |α| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs, Real.sqrt_le_sqrt).

2. Definiteness: if α(e_I) = 0 for every strictly increasing I, then α = 0.
(a) First, α(e_J) = 0 for every J : Fin n → Fin P.
- If J is not injective, then J(i) = J(j) for some i ≠ j. So the tuple e_J has two equal entries, and α(e_J) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective).
- If J is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort J. This is a permutation of Fin n with J∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). J∘σ is injective, hence strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective), so α(e_{J∘σ}) = 0 by hypothesis. Since e_{J∘σ} = e_J∘σ, alternation gives 0 = α(e_J∘σ) = sign(σ)·α(e_J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). As sign(σ) = ±1 is invertible, α(e_J) = 0.
(b) Now take any v = (v_1, …, v_n) and expand v_i = Σ_j v_i(j)·e_j (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr). Multilinearity gives α(v) = Σ_{r : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i v_i(r(i)))·α(e_r) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_sum, map_smul_univ). Every α(e_r) = 0 by (a), so α = 0.

3. Properties of |·|.
(i) |·| is continuous on V: α ↦ α(e_I) is evaluation at a fixed tuple (continuous_eval_const), and squares, finite sums and √ are continuous.
(ii) |tα| = |t|·|α|: every summand gains the factor t², and √(t²S) = |t|√S (Finset.mul_sum, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
(iii) |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
(iv) If |α| = 0 then α = 0: by step 1, |α(e_I)| ≤ 0 for every strictly increasing I, so step 2 applies.

4. Finite dimension and norm comparison. Let L : V → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) be the linear map with (Lα)(I) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing and 0 otherwise.
- L is injective by step 2, and its target is finite-dimensional. So V is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective) and hence a proper metric space (FiniteDimensional.proper_real).
- L is antilipschitz: there is K > 0 with ‖α‖ ≤ K‖Lα‖ for all α (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith with ker L = ⊥, applied to the points 0 and α).
- The target carries the sup norm. Each coordinate of Lα has absolute value at most |α|, by step 1 or because it is 0 ≤ |α|. So ‖Lα‖ ≤ |α| (pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg).
Therefore ‖α‖ ≤ K|α| for all α ∈ V.

5. Compact unit ball. B := {β ∈ V : |β| ≤ 1} is closed by step 3(i). It is bounded because ‖β‖ ≤ K on B by step 4. As V is proper, B is compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). Also 0 ∈ B (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero).

6. Definition of N. For an n-vector ζ, the set ζ(B) ⊆ ℝ is compact (a continuous image) and nonempty. Define N(ζ) := sup ζ(B).
- N(ζ) ∈ ζ(B) (IsCompact.sSup_mem): there is β ∈ B, i.e. |β| ≤ 1, with ζ(β) = N(ζ). This is clause (iv).
- ζ(β') ≤ N(ζ) for every β' ∈ B (le_csSup; ζ(B) is bounded above by compactness).

7. Nonnegativity. 0 ∈ B and ζ(0) = 0, so N(ζ) ≥ 0. This is clause (ii).

8. Domination. If |α| = 0, then α = 0 by step 3(iv), and both sides of |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)|α| are 0. Otherwise let β := |α|⁻¹α. Then |β| = 1 by step 3(ii), so β ∈ B, and −β ∈ B by step 3(iii). Since α = |α|β, we get ζ(α) = |α|ζ(β) ≤ |α|N(ζ) and −ζ(α) = |α|ζ(−β) ≤ |α|N(ζ). Hence |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)|α|. This is clause (iii).

9. Continuity. For n-vectors ζ, ζ' pick β ∈ B with ζ(β) = N(ζ) (step 6). Then N(ζ) = ζ'(β) + (ζ − ζ')(β) ≤ N(ζ') + ‖ζ − ζ'‖·‖β‖ ≤ N(ζ') + K‖ζ − ζ'‖. This uses three facts: ζ'(β) ≤ N(ζ') (step 6), the operator-norm bound (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm), and ‖β‖ ≤ K|β| ≤ K (step 4). By symmetry |N(ζ) − N(ζ')| ≤ K‖ζ − ζ'‖. So N is K-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_le_add_mul'), hence continuous. This is clause (i).

Steps 6–9 give all four clauses. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coordinate bound |α(e_I)| ≤ |α|. Definiteness: α vanishes if all its strictly increasing coordinates vanish (sorting permutation, alternation, multilinear expansion).
The coordinate map L is injective, so covectors are finite-dimensional and ‖α‖ ≤ K|α|; the unit ball B = {|β| ≤ 1} is compact.
N(ζ) := sup ζ(B) is attained and nonnegative, and |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)|α| by rescaling α to |α|⁻¹α ∈ B.
N is K-Lipschitz for the operator norm, hence continuous.

subproblems.title: The mass identity forces the representing n-vector field to attain 1 on the unit covector ball almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Γ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), and μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(ℝ^P) < ∞ and M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) = Γ.massOn ℝ^P = μ(ℝ^P). Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and all n-covectors α (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm), and suppose Γ(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every test n-form ω on ℝ^P. Then for μ-a.e. x there is an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Γ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), μ univ < ∞ → Γ.massOn univ = μ univ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Γ ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ξ x β = 1

subproblems.title: Positive lower n-density of a finite measure on a set forces finite Hⁿ-measure (Vitali 5r-covering)

subproblems.title: Radon–Nikodym density on a positive carrier: μ ≪ ν⌞M₀ with ν(M₀) < ∞ gives μ = (ν⌞M)·θ with θ > 0 on M ⊆ M₀

2. Absolute continuity μ ≪ ν₀. Let ν₀(E) = 0. Since M₀ is Borel, ν₀(E) = ν(E ∩ M₀) (Measure.restrict_apply'), so μ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 by hypothesis. Also μ(E ∩ M₀ᶜ) ≤ μ(M₀ᶜ) = 0. As E ⊆ (E ∩ M₀) ∪ (E ∩ M₀ᶜ), subadditivity gives μ(E) = 0.

(Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top).

   - M := M₀ ∩ {x : 0 < h(x)} ∩ {x : h(x) < ∞} is Borel (measurableSet_lt) and M ⊆ M₀.
